name: RealVNC Connect
description: The commercial, managed evolution of VNC — RealVNC Server, RealVNC Viewer, and a cloud connection broker bundled into one subscription product, with proper encryption, 2FA, file transfer, and centralized administration.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: RealVNC Server requires X11; e.g. Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm users must switch display servers

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: Lossless encoding modes exist, but adaptive JPEG-based Tight-style compression is used for performance

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: No official published fixed FPS figure; performance is network/CPU dependent

Session Recording.comment: Paid tiers can record sessions to WebM format

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Adjusts compression/quality automatically based on available bandwidth

H.264 Codec.comment: Still fundamentally RFB pixel encoding, not a video codec

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Attaches to one existing desktop session, not isolated multi-user terminal sessions

Tailscale Support.comment: No native integration; RealVNC has its own cloud relay/connection broker instead

Open Source.comment: Closed-source commercial product, though built on the open RFB protocol

Microphone Passthrough.comment: The underlying RFB protocol has no built-in audio channel

Pre-Login Access.comment: Supported on Windows when RealVNC Server runs in Service Mode

No Account Required.comment: Cloud-routed connections require a RealVNC account on both ends

2FA / MFA.comment: Email-based 2FA by default, plus optional TOTP and SSO for teams

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Requires falling back to X11; no native Wayland capture support

Web Browser: Client.comment: No clearly confirmed official browser-based viewer

Free Tier.comment: Free for personal use with a limited number of devices

Personal: Monthly.comment: Essentials-tier per-user pricing; a per-device model (~$3.69/mo) is also offered

Team / Business: Monthly.status: Plus / Premium tiers, priced per user or per device

Enterprise.comment: Adds SSO, up to 256-bit AES encryption, and centralized fleet management
